chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿUbayd Allāh informed me, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:

Sajdah is upon seven bones: the forehead, the two hands, the two knees, and the two big toes; and you press your nose down as an act of irghām. As for what is obligatory, it is these seven; and as for the irghām, it is a sunnah (prophetic tradition) from the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

key_terms.الْإِبْهَامَيْنِ: the two big toes, counted among the obligatory points in sajdah
key_terms.الْإِرْغَامُ: pressing the nose down in prostration
key_terms.الْجَبْهَةِ: the forehead, one of the obligatory points of prostration
key_terms.الْفَرْضُ: that which is obligatory and legally required
key_terms.سَبْعَةِ أَعْظُمٍ: seven bones or bodily points upon which sajdah is performed
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not obligatory

ai.seo_question: What body parts are obligatory in sajdah, and is placing the nose on the ground required?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the required points of contact in sajdah during salat (prayer), identifying seven bodily parts as obligatory. It also distinguishes between the obligatory elements of prostration and the recommended practice of placing the nose down, presenting the latter as a sunnah (prophetic tradition) of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
